input.question: What is the reason for morning sickness and other"symptoms" in pregnant women? What, if any, are the advantages to us as a species?
input.ground_truth: (Biologist) Pregnancy sickness prevents the mother ingesting harmful toxins that could damage the embryo. As the embryo is developing (internal organs, limbs etc.) it is incredibly sensitive to toxins that would usually have no effect, e.g. asparagus is fatal to hamster embryos but is a perfectly suitable food for adults. Pregnancy sickness causes retching when these toxins (usually bitter tasting) are detected. It is incredibly useful: women who experience pregnancy sickness (about 75%) are half as likely to have a miscarriage than women who don't.

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

Okay! Imagine a tiny seed wants to grow into a big plant inside a mommy’s tummy. When the seed (which is a baby) starts growing, it can make the mommy feel a little funny. Sometimes her tummy might feel icky or she might want to throw up. That’s called morning sickness.

The funny feelings happen because the baby is growing and changing things in the mommy’s body. It’s like when you have a new friend and everything feels a little different and exciting (but sometimes a little scary too!).

Now, why is this good for people? Well, a long time ago, when humans didn’t know much about babies, these funny feelings helped them know that a baby was coming. It was a sign that something special was happening inside. Also, sometimes, these feelings might help the mommy avoid things that could hurt the baby, like certain foods or things that aren’t good.

So, even though it’s not fun, it helps the baby grow safe and healthy, and it helps the mommy know there’s a baby on the way!
